 CORAM:HONOURABLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MRS. JUSTICE  SUNITA AGARWAL  and  HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ANIRUDDHA P. MAYEE  Date : 14/03/2024  ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MRS. JUSTICE SUNITA AGARWAL)
Both the petitions are raising the common issue with regard to deprivation of the petitioners from their landed property without adopting due process of law.
By our earlier order date 4.12.2023, we have tagged both the petitions.

They have been heard together and are being disposed of by this common Thakor Ranchhodji Pasaji vs Special Land Acquisition Officer on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22350517/
1 judgment and order.
2. From the affidavit of the Secretary, Revenue Department dated 6th January, 2024, it is evident that the possession of the land-in-question belonging to the petitioners herein, has been taken in the year 2011 by NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/7084/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/03/2024 undefined paying some lumpsum compensation as advance compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is evident that the proposal for acquisition of the land-in-question which has been utilised for the purpose of Chandrasan Direct Minor Canal passing through village Chandrasan, the possession of which was taken in the year 2011 by paying some lumpsum compensation as advance compensation, is pending since the year 2009.

It is stated in paragraph No. 6.1 of the affidavit that proposal for the acquisition vide M.R.No.
545/2009 was pending and the same was sent by the acquiring body for the purpose of verification of the lands and identification of the lands to the Additional District Inspector of Land Records, Unit No.1, Ahmedabad on 20.04.2018.

In paragraph No. 6.2, it was further stated that only upon receipt of clear details from the office of the DILR, proper proposal could have been made to the Land Acquisition Officer for the purpose of acquiring the land.

However, as there was no formal acquisition process carried out before promulgation or notification of new survey numbers, the acquiring body could not have proceeded on the basis of the old identification of the lands, since while hearing the objections, interested land owners and occupants were required to be called for as per records as available on the date of acquisition proceedings.
NEUT  C/SCA/7084/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/03/2024  undef 3.

It is, thus, contended that in view of the new enactment, the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 the proceedings are required to be carried out.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As the old proposal, namely M.R.No.545/2009 had as many as 49 Survey Numbers admessuring 2.36.46 H-Sq.Mtrs., it would create a legal impediment if the proceedings are initiated on the basis of old identification and would result into dispute of claims.
It is, thus,
contended that the DILR was directed to prepare occupancy forms, measurement sheet and other relevant statements vide communications dated 10.08.2023 and 06.10.2023.

On 7.12.2023, a joint Thakor Ranchhodji Pasaji vs Special Land Acquisition Officer on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22350517/
2 survey of the lands in question was carried out with a view to identify the discrepancies pertaining to the occupancy in the land holdings and Rojkam had been prepared.

sentences.text: All details were thereafter received by the acquiring body on 2.1.2024 from the Additional DILR and the land acquisition proceedings are to be undertaken accordingly.

Further details of certain communications made between the Executive Engineer, Narmada Yojna Narmada Development N..9, Sanand Chandrasan Minor and the Revenue Department/Additional Collector, Sardar Sarovar Nigam (Narmada),
Ahmedabad have been referred to in paragraph Nos. '7.1' to '7.15'.
However, none of the copies of such communications, as referred in those paragraphs have been appended with the affidavit.
NEUTRA  C/SCA/7084/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/03/2024
undefin 4.

It is contended in paragraph No. 10 of the affidavit that for the purpose of Chandrasan Direct Minor Canal, the lands were acquired in the year 2009-2010 by making lumpsum compensation in advance as agreed between the acquiring authorities and the land owners, whose lands were to be acquired.
There is reference of some circular dated 4.3.2014 to provide steps to be taken in the pending cases of acquisition.

There is reference of communication made to all the Collectors,
Officers on Special Duty (GIDC), Deputy Secretary (Rehb), Narmada Water Supplies and Water Resources and Kalpsar Department and all Special Land Acquisition Officers (ONGC), on the issue of delay in initiating and completing the acquisition proceedings after the said fact came to the notice of the Revenue Authorities on 12.4.2023.

entities.text: Narmada Water Supplies and Water Resources and Kalpsar Department
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is also stated therein that it has come to the notice of the department that in numerous land acquisition cases, which have reached at the stage of Sections 4 and 6 of the Act, necessary steps are required to be taken to expedite the same and to pay compensation accordingly.
A communication dated 12.4.2023 issued by the Secretary, Revenue Department, is appended as Annexure 'IV' at page No. '120' of the paper book.

5. Be that as it may, from the averments in the affidavit noted hereinabove, it is more than evident that the petitioners have been NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/7084/2023 ORDER DATED:
14/03/2024 undefined deprived of the landed property since 2011 without adopting due process of law.

The petitioners had been dispossessed of the landed property by paying some lumpsum compensation as advance compensation on the assurance that their lands would be required and the compensation would be paid after undertaking procedure required under the Land Acquisition Act.

3 6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The instant petition has been filed in the month of April, 2023.
The Notice on the petition was issued on 25.4.2023.
By order dated 4.12.2023, noticing that the correct facts have not been brought on record by the respondents, we required the Secretary, Revenue Department to file his personal affidavit.

7. From the contents of the personal affidavit of the Revenue Secretary noted hereinabove, it is evident that the State and the acquiring body have delayed the matter of acquisition of the land-in-question.
The communications between the State Government and the acquiring body are of the year 2023, i.e. only after the writ petition has been filed and notice has been issued on 25.4.2023.

From the statement made in the affidavit of the Secretary, Revenue Department noted hereinabove, nothing has been done in the matter uptill the month of October, 2023 though proposal was received by the Revenue Department in the year NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/7084/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/03/2024 undefined 2009.
The reference to various communications in the affidavit from paragraph Nos. 7.1 to 7.15 is liable to be ignored, as none of the communications have been brought on record.
8. It is more than evident that there is an apathy on the part of the Revenue Department and the acquiring body.
The poor farmers have been forced to run to the court to seek their legitimate right of compensation for deprivation of their landed property for a period of more than 12 years.
No clear answer came forth from the stand taken by the State department.
We take a strong exception to this approach and direct the Revenue Secretary to take stock of the situation which has come to his notice on 12.4.2023, as admitted by him in his affidavit.

The remedial measures to address the grievance of the land holders whose constitutional right to property under Article 300A of the Constitution has been infringed, shall be undertaken at the earliest.

9. As regards the present petitioners are concerned, the acquisition proceedings by adopting the procedure prescribed under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 to regularise the acquisition of the land in question, shall be undertaken and be positively completed within a period of three months from today with the making of the award.

10. It is clarified that the date of determination of market value of the landed property-in-question,
possession of which has been taken in the year 2011 without adopting due process of law, shall be the date of publication of preliminary notification under Section 11 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 .

sentences.text: All the elements of compensation under the Act, 2013 shall be computed on the market value in accordance with the provisions of the Act, 2013 including statutory interest under Section 80 of the said Act.
11. With the above observations, the writ petitions stand disposed of.

It is, however, provided that for any further inaction on the part of the respondents, delay in undertaking acquisition proceedings, non-making of the award within the time given above, it would be open for the Thakor Ranchhodji Pasaji vs Special Land Acquisition Officer on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22350517/
4 petitioner to approach this court.
